idea: I record birdsong at fixed spots every week and my recordings are a mess of files on three drives. I want a catalog for the recordings and what I identified in them, so the collection is finally usable.

problem: I cannot answer even simple questions like which species I heard at the reservoir last spring; finding anything means opening dozens of files.
user: Just me for entry; a university contact might one day want exports, but she would never use the tool herself.
workflow: After each session I copy files off the recorder, tag each with site, date, weather, and species heard, and later search by any of those.
success: The real test is retrieval: any species-site-season question answered in under a minute, for the whole back catalog.
data: About 4,000 WAV files, 30 to 300 MB each, across three external drives; the catalog should reference files where they live rather than move them.
Species tags follow a standard checklist; sites are a fixed list of nine locations I survey.
operations: The drives travel with me; the catalog must tell me when a referenced drive is not plugged in instead of erroring.
